title: NI-MSME Supports MSME Growth Through Skill Development, Innovation & Entrepreneurship
excerpt: NI-MSME Supports MSME Growth Through Skill Development, Innovation & Entrepreneurship New Delhi, Oct 22 (KNN) The National Institute for Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (ni-msme), under the Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises, has conducted 17,672 programmes in India, benefiting 6,07,497 participants, according to data released by the institute. The institute has also conducted 550 international training programmes, training 11,032 executives from 150 countries. Its other activities include 6,840 skill development programmes for 2,10,062 youth, implementation of 27 MSME cluster development projects, 235 services through Intellectual Property Facilitation Centres and completion of 962 research studies. Established in 1960, ni-msme provides training, research, consultancy and capacity-building support in areas including entrepreneurship, finance, marketing, international trade, digital transformation and technology adoption. The institute received a three-star “Utkrisht” rating from the Capacity Building Commission. In March 2026, the institute organised national conferences on digital marketing, AI automation and e-commerce, and on digital-enabled factories and Industry 5.0, covering technologies such as artificial intelligence, the Industrial Internet of Things and cloud computing. Under a NABARD-supported initiative, Amarchintha Handloom Weavers Producer Company Ltd. in Telangana received digital marketing training and subsequent handholding support through the institute. The company reported securing an order worth Rs16 lakh through Google, while its annual turnover reached Rs2.8 crore. Another beneficiary, woman entrepreneur Sunkishala Swarupa of Telangana, received training in digital branding and marketing for her millet-based food business. According to the institute, her monthly turnover increased from Rs20,000 to Rs2 lakh, and the enterprise generated employment for local women. (KNN Bureau)

title: 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum to be held in Samvidhan Sadan on October 26-27: Lok Sabha Speaker
excerpt: New Delhi [India], October 22 : The Parliament of India will host the 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum on October 26 and 27 in the Central Hall of Samvidhan Sadan. The conference will be inaugurated on October 26. Addressing a press conference at Parliament House on Thursday, Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla said that the conference marks a new chapter in the history of India's parliamentary diplomacy. It will bring together Presiding Officers and parliamentary leaders from BRICS member and partner countries, Union Ministers, Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha Harivansh, Presiding Officers of State Legislatures, Members of Parliament and other dignitaries. The Lok Sabha Speaker stated that Prime Minister Narendra Modi would grace the event and meet the leaders of the visiting delegations. He further stated that the conference would feature bilateral and multilateral interactions with the leaders of visiting delegations and parliamentary friendship groups. A meeting of the Secretaries of the delegations will be held on 25 October 2026 to finalise the Joint Statement of the 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum. Highlighting the central theme of the programme, he said that the Forum would deliberate on the overarching theme of “Strengthening Parliaments for People-Centric Development". He added that, building on the legacy of the BRICS Parliamentary Forum, the 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum would facilitate consensus-based dialogue through the following four high-level sessions: Resilience: The critical role of parliaments in strengthening institutions to ensure a better future; Innovation: Promoting human-centred innovation in artificial intelligence and digital technologies through parliaments; Cooperation: Ensuring a more representative system of global governance through parliamentary cooperation; and Sustainability: The role of parliaments in ensuring a sustainable and inclusive future for our countries. In addition, a special meeting of the Chairpersons of the International Affairs Committees of the parliaments of BRICS member and partner countries will be held to deliberate on parliamentary diplomacy, capacity building and the exchange of best practices. Birla further stated that, alongside high-level plenary sessions, parallel meetings and bilateral exchanges, the conference would also feature a cultural programme. The Vice-President of India will host a banquet in honour of the distinguished guests. Members of the delegations will visit the Parliament of India and also enjoy cultural visits in Delhi. The conference will conclude on October 27. (ANI)

title: Ports, Shipping, and Waterways Minister Sonowal invites Polish firms to build, innovate, and invest in India
excerpt: Union Ports, Shipping & Waterways Minister Sarbananda Sonowal on Thursday urged Polish companies to "build, innovate, and invest in India" rather than only sell to it, as he pitched the country's growth story to business leaders from both nations. Addressing the India-Poland Business Forum here, Sonowal proposed a Startup Bridge, an Innovation Corridor, and an AI and Quantum Dialogue to link businesses, researchers, and innovators in both countries. Trade between the two countries has reached $6.36 billion, and Indian investment in Poland exceeds $3 billion. Polish companies are also active in India in packaging, manufacturing, waste-to-energy and electric mobility. The ambition should be larger than doubling trade by 2030, he added."We should create together. We should innovate together. We should invest together. We should build trusted supply chains together. And we should succeed together," Sonowal said. He urged business leaders to see the India-EU free trade agreement as more than a trade pact. "View it as a partnership multiplier," he said. It opens a larger window into the Indian market for Polish firms, he said, and widens European opportunities for Indian ones. He further stated that when Prime Minister Narendra Modi visited Poland in August 2024, he and Prime Minister Tusk elevated the bilateral relations to a Strategic Partnership. They did so with a clear conviction: the India-Poland relationship must not only be strong in diplomacy; it must also be strong in business, technology, investment and innovation, he added. The aim now, he said, is for the relationship to be as strong in business, technology, investment and innovation as it is in diplomacy."India offers the scale of a large and growing market, the skills of a young and talented workforce, and the trust of a democracy committed to reform, enterprise, and openness," Sonowal said. The minister stated that the two economies fit together. Poland has strengths in engineering, machinery, mining technologies, transport, environmental solutions, and advanced manufacturing, while India has the market, talent, and manufacturing base to give those capabilities scale. Sonowal highlighted that India has set an ambitious target to generate 500 GW of non-fossil fuel power capacity by 2030, putting forth a strong Climate Action step by the country. He put the investment needed at roughly 280 billion to 300 billion euros, with openings for equipment makers, storage, power grids, green hydrogen, recycling and environmental technology. Poland's experience in mining, critical minerals and clean energy could help, Sonowal said. On technology, he noted that Indian IT companies have made Poland a base for their European operations and employ about 10,000 people there. He said the next step should go beyond IT services, into artificial intelligence, quantum computing, 5G applications, digital infrastructure, smart manufacturing and space.

title: Rajasthan’s entrepreneurial energy, Gujarat’s innovation ecosystem can create magic for youth’: Minister Bavaliya
excerpt: Jaipur, Oct 22 (IANS) The Government of Gujarat on Thursday invited Rajasthan’s business community to explore investment opportunities in the state at a roadshow in Jaipur ahead of the Vibrant Gujarat Global Summit (VGGS) 2027, scheduled to be held from January 10-12 at Mahatma Mandir, Gandhinagar. The roadshow brought together industrialists, traders and business representatives from across Rajasthan, providing a platform to explore investment opportunities and potential partnerships between the two neighbouring states. The Gujarat delegation also held one-on-one meetings with industry representatives, highlighting the state’s business-friendly policies, infrastructure, industrial ecosystem and government support for investors. Gujarat Minister of State Kunvarjibhai Bavaliya, who holds the portfolios of Labour, Skill Development and Employment, and Rural Development, spoke exclusively to IANS in an e-interview. Custom Ad: Multiplex Excerpts: IANS: How do you see the relationship between Rajasthan and Gujarat? Kunvarjibhai Bavaliya: The relationship between Rajasthan and Gujarat is not new. A long shared border, centuries of trade and cultural exchange form its foundation. Shrinathji of Nathdwara and Dwarkadhish, this bond of faith connects thousands of devotees between the two states every year. IANS. How have the two states worked together in trade and enterprise? Kunvarjibhai Bavaliya: For generations, Gujarati and Marwari entrepreneurs have together built successful enterprises in trade, manufacturing, finance and exports. IANS. You greeted Rajasthan with "Khamma Ghani". What is the sentiment behind it? Kunvarjibhai Bavaliya: For me, "Khamma Ghani" is not just a greeting. It is a message of friendship from Gujarat to Rajasthan. IANS. How do you see Rajasthan and Jaipur today? Kunvarjibhai Bavaliya: Rajasthan today is one of the country's most dynamic centres of growth. Jaipur, while preserving its heritage, is emerging as a hub of business, technology and innovation. IANS. What concrete benefits can Rajasthan's industries gain from working with Gujarat? Kunvarjibhai Bavaliya: Gujarat is India's export gateway. Its ports and logistics give Rajasthan's manufacturing strength a natural route to global markets. The Delhi-Mumbai Industrial Corridor, which runs through both states, is a shared economic corridor linking manufacturing hubs, logistics parks and export gateways. IANS. Which industries of the future is Gujarat focusing on? Kunvarjibhai Bavaliya: Gujarat is building not only the industries of today but also the industries of tomorrow. Through the Viksit Gujarat Industrial Policy 2026, our focus is on semiconductors, electronics, GCCs, AI and advanced manufacturing. IANS. Where does Gujarat stand in semiconductors, and what opportunity does this hold for Rajasthan? Kunvarjibhai Bavaliya: Six of the 12 projects approved under the India Semiconductor Mission are in Gujarat. This is not just about chips; it is an entire ecosystem, with opportunities for Rajasthan's enterprises as well. IANS. What roles do Dholera and Khavda play in this growth story? Kunvarjibhai Bavaliya: The Dholera Special Investment Region is becoming a leading destination for high-tech industries. The Khavda Renewable Energy Park is making Gujarat a frontrunner in clean energy. IANS. How can the two states come together in traditional sectors such as gems and jewellery, and textiles? Kunvarjibhai Bavaliya: Jaipur's world-famous gem industry complements Surat's diamond processing and lab-grown diamonds. Similarly, Rajasthan's strength in wool, weaving and apparel, combined with Gujarat's leadership in fibre, fabric and technical textiles, reaches global markets. IANS: What is the potential for partnership in renewable energy? Kunvarjibhai Bavaliya: Rajasthan's leadership in solar energy and Gujarat's Khavda ecosystem can together create new opportunities in clean energy manufacturing, green hydrogen and green ammonia. IASN. How can cooperation grow in ceramics and tourism? Kunvarjibhai Bavaliya: Rajasthan's mineral wealth complements Morbi's ceramics cluster. And the shared heritage of the two states can give rise to integrated tourism circuits. IANS. How will large investments benefit small businesses and ordinary people? Kunvarjibhai Bavaliya: Large investments create supplier networks; supplier networks create opportunities for MSMEs, and MSMEs become the engine of employment and inclusive growth. IANS. As Minister of Labour and Skills, how do you see the link between investment and skills? Kunvarjibhai Bavaliya: I believe that the future competitiveness of any economy depends as much on talent and skills as it does on investment. IANS: How is Gujarat preparing its young people for the future? Kunvarjibhai Bavaliya: Gujarat's goal is to prepare young people not just for jobs, but for leadership in the industries of the future. For this, we are investing continuously in skills, research and industry-academia collaboration. IANS: What does this partnership hold for young people in both states? Kunvarjibhai Bavaliya: Rajasthan's entrepreneurial energy and Gujarat's innovation ecosystem can together create immense opportunities for the country's youth. This partnership is not only about investment, but it is about creating jobs, driving innovation, strengthening MSMEs and building world-class value chains. --IANS arc/dan
